hints.title: Stone Remainder Periodicity
hints.text: Players can take between 1 and 3 stones on their turn. If you face 4 stones, any move leaves the opponent with 1, 2, or 3 stones, resulting in a loss.

hints.title: Four-Step Cycle Invariance
hints.text: For any heap size that is a multiple of 4, the second player can always mirror moves to maintain the multiple of 4 until reaching 4.

hints.title: Single Modulo Divisibility Test
hints.text: You can guarantee a win if and only if n is not divisible by 4. Return n modulo 4 is nonzero.

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive game state simulation or memoized search times out for large n and overflows call stack.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Mathematical periodic equivalence reduces the entire game to a single modulo check in O(1) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the game theory pattern and deduce the periodicity of winning positions.
